episodes.195560: A secondary front crossing the region amid an already fall-like air mass over seasonably mild lake waters led to the development of a brief line of showers and a few rumbles of thunder. This line also included a brief waterspout over Little Traverse Bay.
episodes.196672: The interaction of Hurricane Kirk and another low pressure across the north Atlantic modulated the local weather pattern, pooling abundant moisture and promoting light winds in the region. Additionally, increasing instability due to the proximity of a mid to upper level trough favored deeper convection development each afternoon. This resulted in widespread showers and thunderstorms each day along Puerto Rico, with daily amounts ranging from 2 to 4 inches, and localized higher amounts. With an elevated flooding risk, several flood and landslide reports were received.
episodes.196744: Large rainbands associated with a low pressure area near South Florida (not associated with Hurricane Milton in the southern Gulf of Mexico) entered the Atlantic metro areas of South Florida bringing heavy rain and multiple round of showers overnight October 6th into the morning of the 7th. With a very moist vertical profile and instability, this kept in place favorable conditions for the showers to develop and a Flood Watch remained in effect for the entire area.
episodes.196934: On the evening of October 6th, a cold front promoted isolated showers and thunderstorms across West Virginia. One particular storm that evening crossed through both Ritchie and Doddridge Counties and resulted in downed trees due to the strong winds it caused. With the loss of daytime heating, radar activity quickly weakened in the state and departed to the east.
episodes.196935: A cold front sweeping through southeast Ohio during the late afternoon of October 6th led to an isolated instance of storm damage in Vinton County. Several trees and power lines were knocked down by the strong winds associated with passing convection aligned along the front. Storms then quickly shifted off to the east for the evening.
episodes.196955: On Sunday October 6th, severe thunderstorms developed within the warm sector of a nearby passing area of low pressure. A pre-frontal trough along with increased instability and shear values caused thunderstorms to develop as the trough tracked into far western New York. As the trough and thunderstorms continued east from near Lake Erie, the increased instability over land, along with around 50 knots of bulk shear, caused the thunderstorms to expand in coverage and strength. Damaging thunderstorm winds and large hail were reported from interior portions of the Western Southern Tier, northeast to near Batavia and to near Rochester. Thunderstorms weakened as they tracked east into the Northern Finger Lakes and points east as instability and shear decreased.
episodes.197217: Widespread showers and thunderstorms impacted the Florida Keys, with isolated gale-force thunderstorm wind gusts occurring near the Lower Keys.  Weak non-tropical low pressure was located over the east-central Gulf of Mexico moving slowly eastward.
episodes.197218: A trough of low pressure combined with favorable upper level divergence supported strong convective development across the Straits of Florida and Florida Keys.  Scattered gale-force wind gusts occurred in association with widespread showers and thunderstorms moving eastward through the Florida Keys.
episodes.197485: Strong southwesterly wind ahead of an approaching front eventually advected sufficient moisture and warm air in the lower levels to overcome a capping inversion ahead of a cold front that would eventually be the  main driver of forcing to take advantage of a supportive environment. Damaging wind was the primary threat, although the shear and lapse rates aloft pointed towards a limited potential for large hail as well. Tornadoes looked possible, however, LCLs were relatively high, and any issued TORs did not verify.

The City of Miami Beach Emergency Manager reported flooding across several roadways in Miami Beach due to heavy rainfall in the area. The South Florida Water Management District estimated 3 to 5 inches of rain in this general area from late October 6th through 7th. Photo evidence showed several inches of rain ponding on the roadways into inclined driveways. Clogged drains may have played a significant role in standing water during this period.
